finding.claim: With the default allow_remote_refs=None, a schema's local $ref (relative or file://) may resolve to a file outside the input base path. The file is read and parsed, and its contents are rendered into generated Python models. This is a local file disclosure through untrusted schema input. It only warns (deprecation) and is not blocked by default.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled schema file or URL content (e.g. a $ref value such as "../../../etc/app/secrets.yaml" or "file:///home/victim/.config/x.yaml") in a schema the victim runs the generator on with default flags.
finding.sink: Path.read_bytes / _load_ref_data_from_path in jsonschema.py:11002-11020, and generated model output (field names, defaults, enum values, descriptions) written by the generator.

trace.note: _get_ref_body_from_remote builds full_path = base_path / resolved_ref (joined, so '..' is not normalized away) and calls _resolve_local_ref_path.
_resolve_local_ref_path resolves the path. The containment check at 10978 is short-circuited by 'or self.allow_remote_refs is True' and fails only when the value is False.
When allow_remote_refs is None (the default), an outside-base path only triggers warn_deprecated and returns resolved_path (line 10990). The file is loaded.
The resolved path is read via _load_ref_data_from_path (11002) and parsed as YAML/JSON. Parse errors are wrapped in InvalidFileFormatError, which may echo file content.
The same gate is reached for file:// refs (11071-11085), so absolute paths are also readable by default.

finding.guards_checked: (1) Containment check at 10978: it is bypassed when allow_remote_refs is None or True. Only False blocks it (10992+). (2) Config default: config.py:229 and base_config.py:172 default to None. __main__.py:2970 only sets True when --url is used. (3) Content must parse as a YAML/JSON mapping (11002-11014), so arbitrary binary files fail. The file's keys and values still flow into output. (4) Remote HTTP refs are separately guarded (http.py _validate_url_for_fetch, DNS pinning, redirect checks) and are not part of this finding. Severity caveat: the project marks this as a deprecation transition (behavior.remote-ref-default). Reachability needs a victim who generates code from an untrusted or third-party schema with default flags, and disclosure needs the attacker to see the output (e.g. a service returning generated code, or a committed artifact). I did not run the tool to confirm end-to-end; the finding is from code reading.
